Proposal A

Choice 1

Preamble

This proposal aims to expressly forbid any contributions to Debian written with the use or assistance of large language models (LLMs) or other generative AI tools.

The scope of this GR is (non-exhaustive):

  • Debian source packages
  • Official Debian project software, such as lintian
  • Debian web resources
  • Documentation and translations added by Debian contributors
  • Official communication from Debian

It does not include:

  • Upstream projects using LLMs for development
  • AI-related software
  • Upstream patches/security fixes etc.

Rationale

Debian has a well-earned reputation for stability. This stability is crucial to Debian's position in the free software ecosystem. It is our belief that widespread LLM usage comes from the "move fast, and break things" attitude that, while common in many parts of this industry, is contrary to what makes Debian Debian, and is inappropriate for Debian contributors.

In practical terms, LLM usage raises the following concerns:

1. Copyright

LLM output has very unclear legal status: it may be possible to copyright on its own merits, or not; it may be affected by all of the licenses and copyrights in the training data, or not. Debian Policy and the DFSG require absolute clarity for licensing and copyright[1][2]. Software and other contributions written conventionally by humans with unclear copyright or license status are not allowed in Debian; LLM output should not have a special exception to this.

2. Quality

LLM output has many well-known problems with accuracy.[3][4][5] A LLM can never "know" if its output is correct since it merely produces syntactically likely combinations of the training data. In some environments this is good enough. In Debian, it is not. For instance, in packaging, each Debian source package is unique. Since packaging syntax and best practices have changed over time, a LLM-produced package will have a mixture of contents spanning the age of the archive, with watch files that do not work, overrides out of context, imaginary copyright, and will generally be unfit for upload. A seasoned Debian contributor with packaging expertise may find some limited usefulness here, but a new contributor cannot, and would not know how to fix it. These same quality and accuracy concerns apply clearly to all of the areas listed in the scope of this proposal above. If Debian were a closed organization comprising only domain experts who never leave, this might not be an issue; however,

3. Community

Debian is a project that is more than just code: it is a community built on shared interests in free software and solving technical problems. Debian intentionally grows this community through many means, and new contributors are always encouraged to join. Allowing LLM contributions breaks this. New contributors submitting LLM output for review places an unnecessary strain on the reviewer, which can lead to burnout. Furthermore, LLM-dependent new contributors do not actually learn and understand the details of Debian packaging or processes, so they cannot come to replace a former burned out DD.

4. Ethics

LLM companies directly hurt the free software community as whole by scraping the whole web for training data without any regard for license, copyright, or even established conventions such as robots.txt.[6] This has had a major negative impact on Debian's public web resources, effectively a large scale and perpetual Denial of Service attack on sites that many users rely on. As a consequence parts of our infrastructure were not reachable at all, and JS-based checks had to be enabled. Many other projects were similarly affected. Furthermore, LLM training consumes a staggering amount of resources[7], and the user verification systems that we have been forced to implement as protection waste resources as well. This is blatant disregard for the internet as a public resource, wastes system administrator time, and although individual LLM sessions do not directly use massive resources or DoS the public web, the fact that they can be used at all is a direct result of these unethical behaviours by the LLM companies.

Debian has a Social Contract. [8] Our priorities are our users and free software. Debian is Stable. [9] Users and organizations choose Debian because it is reliable and secure.

Debian is not here to generate as much code as possible requiring manual review by a shrinking number of human volunteers, or to package every piece of software, or to rush new features, but these are what LLMs are used for.

In conclusion, allowing LLM contributions is contrary to the social contract and the common cause of creating a free operating system with a focus on quality and stability.

Proposal

In the interest of not eroding Debian's reputation or further damaging the community, LLM-assisted contributions should be prohibited from inclusion in Debian.

Though our position is that LLM contributions are contrary to documents already ratified by Debian, in order to remove all doubt, we propose the following addition to the Social Contract:

6. Works Created through the use of Large Language Models (LLMs)

We will not
allow direct contributions to Debian written with the use or assistance of large
language models (LLMs) or other generative AI tools. Direct contributions are
defined as packaging, native Debian software like lintian, documentation and
translations written by Debian contributors, and official Debian web resources,
etc. Other categories such as upstream projects written with LLM assistance may
be included at a later date. This ensures that Debian remains a stable, trusted,
and reliable operating system, and protects the interests of the Debian
volunteers who make it possible.

Possible Issues

Other projects exploring similar decisions have elicited a common reply: "How will you enforce a ban on LLM contributions?" While enforcement could be a challenge, this is a statement of intent by the Debian community, and we trust this community to adhere to it in good faith.

Proposal B

Choice 2

Allow AI-Assisted Contributions

Using its power under Constitution section 4.1 (5), the project issues the following statement describing its current position on AI-assisted contributions. This statement describes the position of the project at the time it is adopted. That position may evolve as time passes without the need to resort to future general resolutions. The GR process remains available if the project needs a decision and cannot come to a consensus.

The Debian project recognizes that AI-assisted contributions raise many concerns, e.g. about the technical quality and maintainability of such contributions, and their legal status. AI itself also raises additional concerns, about its impact on society at large, on the IT industry and on Free Software; about its environmental impact; and the aggressive or non-compliant practices of AI scrapers.

Nevertheless, many Debian contributors find AI tools helpful when contributing to Debian, and ultimately for improving Debian.

Given both the benefits and risks of AI assistance, and the controversial discussions within the community, the Debian project finds it necessary to clarify its position on AI-assisted contributions and establish clear guidelines.

The Debian project allows AI-assisted contributions (partially or fully generated by an LLM), provided the following conditions are met:

  1. Tooling Legal Compatibility: Contributors should ensure that the terms and conditions of the generative AI tool do not impose contractual restrictions that conflict with the distribution, modification, or use of the output in the context of Debian.
  2. Licensing and Attribution: If any pre-existing copyrighted materials (including pre-existing code licensed as free software) authored or owned by third parties are included in the AI tool’s output, prior to contributing such output to the project, the contributor should verify they have the right to submit it under the relevant open source license.
  3. Accountability: Contributors assume full responsibility for their contributions, including vouching for the technical merit, security, license compliance, and utility of their submissions. The contributor remains solely accountable for the entirety of these contributions. Contributors should fully understand the proposed changes and be prepared to justify them.
  4. Disclosure: When a significant portion of a contribution is generated or substantially assisted by a tool, contributors should disclose the use of the tool, making it clearly visible to the intended audience. This covers all forms of contribution, including code, mailing list posts, and bug discussions. The form of the disclosure is left to the contributor; one convenient option for commits is a Git trailer such as Generated-By: or Assisted-By:.
  5. Prior Discussion of Bulk or Automated Changes: Similarly to the mass-bug filing process (Developers Reference section 7.1.1), contributors should discuss their intention before submitting bulk or autonomously generated contributions. Any such automated process should be overseen by a human who remains accountable for its behavior and output.
  6. Confidentiality and Privacy: Contributors must not use generative AI tools that transmit data to untrusted providers with non-public or sensitive project information (such as embargoed security reports or private communication), as this may lead to the unintended disclosure of confidential data.

Proposal C

Choice 3

Summary: Reject LLMs (generative "AI") as far as practical

BACKGROUND

LLMs have many serious problems, including: undermining the mechanisms of free software community building; environmental damage; exploitation of authors; disruption to open web hosting by aggressive scraping; generation and promulgation of bullshit; polluting the information commons; hazards to users' mental health; economic bubbles; distortion of the computer hardware market; fraud; ownership by horrible people and companies; and so on. Ethical and safe use of this technology is almost impossible.

Ideally, LLM output should not form any part of software that we rely on, nor should LLM output ever take the place of human-written prose.

Unfortunately some of the wider software world, including many of our upstreams, take a different view. Therefore a complete ban on LLM output as part of Debian is currently impractical.

REQUESTS

1. We request that all contributors to Debian avoid the use of LLMs in their Debian work.

2. We request that all decisionmakers within Debian discourage LLM use as much as practical. Practicality is a judgement call and we recognise that it will involve uncomfortable compromises.

3. We request that everyone, even outside Debian, should refrain from using this technology. In particular, the Free Software and Open Source communities should reject LLMs. We recognise that not everyone will heed this call.

REQUIREMENTS (SUPPLEMENT TO THE CODE OF CONDUCT)

4. Within Debian, messages to humans (including for example bug reports, mailing list messages, discussions on Salsa, and blog posts on Planet Debian) must be drafted solely by humans without LLM assistance.

5. Any use of LLMs for Debian work must be disclosed.

6. Individual projects and maintainers may ban LLM contributions completely. Such bans (including by upstream projects) must be respected.

7. Violations of these requirements should be treated as violations of the Code of Conduct and should result in swift but proportionate disciplinary action.

8. Any contributor who feels they cannot write in English without assistance, may write in their native language, and expect readers to use translation tools of their choice. In that case a human-written English summary would be very welcome but is not required. In any case we promise not to shame anyone for any linguistic mistakes.

Proposal D

Choice 4

Accept AI contributions for Debian specific work

Debian as a project does not endorse or recommend the use of generative AI assistants for software development, as it raises multiple concerns about ethics, legality, copyright, etc.

Nevertheless, Debian acknowledges that these practices are already in use and here to stay. Rather than banning their use, which seems counter-productive and unenforceable, the project chooses to place responsibility on contributors and therefore defines the following guidelines.

These apply exclusively to code and work done specifically for the Debian project (Debian websites, applications, resources, packages, etc.). They do not apply to any upstream work. In what follows, "work" refers to the contributions done specifically for the Debian project.

  • All code and work assisted by a generative AI agent or tool must comply with the DFSG.
  • The submitter is solely responsible for the submitted work and:
    • they sufficiently evaluated and properly understand the work they intend to submit, and are able to explain and defend it;
    • they put any potential Signed-off-by tag and GPG signatures on the contributions they send to the Debian infrastructure (package, commit, mail, …) themselves;
    • any content uploaded that would end up in production on Debian infrastructure (main git branch, package upload) has been submitted by them explicitely.
  • Work assisted by a generative AI agent or tool should be marked as such in the adapted place (commit message, changelog, …). Some lightweight generative tools, such as tab-completion in Copilot, may be used without the contributor realising they rely on generative AI models; we therefore trust submitters to assess when this rule applies. When in doubt, add such marking;
  • No cloud-based AI shall be used when the data transmitted could either be sensitive to the project (personal data, information under embargo, …) or not public (debian-private discussions, …).

Work assisted by a generative AI agent or tool should be marked as such in the adapted place (commit message, changelog, …). Some lightweight generative tools, such as tab-completion in Copilot, may be used without the contributor realising they rely on generative AI models; we therefore trust submitters to assess when this rule applies. When in doubt, add such marking; No cloud-based AI shall be used when the data transmitted could either be sensitive to the project (personal data, information under embargo, …) or not public (debian-private discussions, …). blocks.html_en: LLM output has many well-known problems with accuracy.[3][4][5] A LLM can never "know" if its output is correct since it merely produces syntactically likely combinations of the training data. sentences.en: Community

blocks.html_en: Debian is a project that is more than just code: it is a community built on shared interests in free software and solving technical problems. Debian intentionally grows this community through many means, and new contributors are always encouraged to join. Allowing LLM contributions breaks this. New contributors submitting LLM output for review places an unnecessary strain on the reviewer, which can lead to burnout. Furthermore, LLM-dependent new contributors do not actually learn and understand the details of Debian packaging or processes, so they cannot come to replace a former burned out DD.

sentences.en: Ethics
sentences.zh: 伦理

blocks.html_en: LLM companies directly hurt the free software community as whole by scraping the whole web for training data without any regard for license, copyright, or even established conventions such as robots.txt.[6] This has had a major negative impact on Debian's public web resources, effectively a large scale and perpetual Denial of Service attack on sites that many users rely on. As a consequence parts of our infrastructure were not reachable at all, and JS-based checks had to be enabled. Many other projects were similarly affected. Furthermore, LLM training consumes a staggering amount of resources[7], and the user verification systems that we have been forced to implement as protection waste resources as well. This is blatant disregard for the internet as a public resource, wastes system administrator time, and although individual LLM sessions do not directly use massive resources or DoS the public web, the fact that they can be used at all is a direct result of these unethical behaviours by the LLM companies.

sentences.en: LLM companies directly hurt the free software community as whole by scraping the whole web for training data without any regard for license, copyright, or even established conventions such as robots.txt.[6] This has had a major negative impact on Debian's public web resources, effectively a large scale and perpetual Denial of Service attack on sites that many users rely on.

sentences.zh: 这是对互联网作为公共资源的公然漠视，浪费了系统管理员的时间，虽然个别LLM课程不直接使用大量资源或DoS公共网络，但它们完全可以使用的事实是LLM公司这些不道德行为的直接结果。

sentences.zh: 本声明描述了该项目在通过时的立场。

sentences.en: That position may evolve as time passes without the need to resort to future general resolutions.
sentences.zh: 这一立场可能会随着时间的推移而演变，而无需诉诸未来的一般性决议。

sentences.en: The GR process remains available if the project needs a decision and cannot come to a consensus.
sentences.zh: 如果项目需要做出决定但无法达成共识，GR 流程仍然可用。

blocks.html_en: The Debian project recognizes that AI-assisted contributions raise many concerns, e.g. about the technical quality and maintainability of such contributions, and their legal status. AI itself also raises additional concerns, about its impact on society at large, on the IT industry and on Free Software; about its environmental impact; and the aggressive or non-compliant practices of AI scrapers.

sentences.en: The Debian project recognizes that AI-assisted contributions raise many concerns, e.g. about the technical quality and maintainability of such contributions, and their legal status.
sentences.zh: Debian 项目认识到人工智能辅助的贡献引起了许多担忧，例如关于此类贡献的技术质量和可维护性及其法律地位。

sentences.en: AI itself also raises additional concerns, about its impact on society at large, on the IT industry and on Free Software; about its environmental impact; and the aggressive or non-compliant practices of AI scrapers.
sentences.zh: 人工智能本身也引发了额外的担忧，即它对整个社会、IT 行业和自由软件的影响；关于其对环境的影响；以及人工智能抓取工具的攻击性或不合规做法。

blocks.html_en: Nevertheless, many Debian contributors find AI tools helpful when contributing to Debian, and ultimately for improving Debian.

sentences.en: Nevertheless, many Debian contributors find AI tools helpful when contributing to Debian, and ultimately for improving Debian.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，许多 Debian 贡献者发现人工智能工具在为 Debian 做出贡献并最终改进 Debian 时很有帮助。

blocks.html_en: Given both the benefits and risks of AI assistance, and the controversial discussions within the community, the Debian project finds it necessary to clarify its position on AI-assisted contributions and establish clear guidelines.

sentences.en: Given both the benefits and risks of AI assistance, and the controversial discussions within the community, the Debian project finds it necessary to clarify its position on AI-assisted contributions and establish clear guidelines.
sentences.zh: 考虑到人工智能辅助的好处和风险，以及社区内有争议的讨论，Debian 项目认为有必要澄清其对人工智能辅助贡献的立场并建立明确的指导方针。

blocks.html_en: The Debian project allows AI-assisted contributions (partially or fully generated by an LLM), provided the following conditions are met:

sentences.en: The Debian project allows AI-assisted contributions (partially or fully generated by an LLM), provided the following conditions are met:
sentences.zh: Debian 项目允许人工智能辅助贡献（部分或全部由法学硕士生成），前提是满足以下条件：

blocks.html_en: • Tooling Legal Compatibility: Contributors should ensure that the terms and conditions of the generative AI tool do not impose contractual restrictions that conflict with the distribution, modification, or use of the output in the context of Debian.

sentences.en: Tooling Legal Compatibility: Contributors should ensure that the terms and conditions of the generative AI tool do not impose contractual restrictions that conflict with the distribution, modification, or use of the output in the context of Debian.
sentences.zh: 工具法律兼容性：贡献者应确保生成式 AI 工具的条款和条件不会施加与 Debian 环境中输出的分发、修改或使用相冲突的合同限制。

blocks.html_en: • Licensing and Attribution: If any pre-existing copyrighted materials (including pre-existing code licensed as free software) authored or owned by third parties are included in the AI tool’s output, prior to contributing such output to the project, the contributor should verify they have the right to submit it under the relevant open source license.

sentences.en: Licensing and Attribution: If any pre-existing copyrighted materials (including pre-existing code licensed as free software) authored or owned by third parties are included in the AI tool’s output, prior to contributing such output to the project, the contributor should verify they have the right to submit it under the relevant open source license.
sentences.zh: 许可和归属：如果人工智能工具的输出中包含由第三方创作或拥有的任何预先存在的受版权保护的材料（包括作为免费软件许可的预先存在的代码），则在将此类输出贡献给项目之前，贡献者应验证他们有权根据相关开源许可提交该输出。

blocks.html_en: • Accountability: Contributors assume full responsibility for their contributions, including vouching for the technical merit, security, license compliance, and utility of their submissions. The contributor remains solely accountable for the entirety of these contributions. Contributors should fully understand the proposed changes and be prepared to justify them.

sentences.en: Accountability: Contributors assume full responsibility for their contributions, including vouching for the technical merit, security, license compliance, and utility of their submissions.
sentences.zh: 责任：贡献者对其贡献承担全部责任，包括保证其提交内容的技术优点、安全性、许可证合规性和实用性。

sentences.en: The contributor remains solely accountable for the entirety of these contributions.
sentences.zh: 贡献者仍然对全部这些贡献承担全部责任。

sentences.en: Contributors should fully understand the proposed changes and be prepared to justify them.
sentences.zh: 贡献者应充分理解提议的更改并准备好证明其合理性。

blocks.html_en: • Disclosure: When a significant portion of a contribution is generated or substantially assisted by a tool, contributors should disclose the use of the tool, making it clearly visible to the intended audience. This covers all forms of contribution, including code, mailing list posts, and bug discussions. The form of the disclosure is left to the contributor; one convenient option for commits is a Git trailer such as Generated-By: or Assisted-By:.

sentences.en: Disclosure: When a significant portion of a contribution is generated or substantially assisted by a tool, contributors should disclose the use of the tool, making it clearly visible to the intended audience.
sentences.zh: 披露：当贡献的很大一部分是由工具生成或实质协助时，贡献者应披露该工具的使用情况，使其对目标受众清晰可见。

sentences.en: This covers all forms of contribution, including code, mailing list posts, and bug discussions.
sentences.zh: 这涵盖了所有形式的贡献，包括代码、邮件列表帖子和错误讨论。

sentences.en: The form of the disclosure is left to the contributor; one convenient option for commits is a Git trailer such as Generated-By: or Assisted-By:.
sentences.zh: 披露的形式由贡献者决定；一种方便的提交选项是 Git 预告片，例如“Generate-By:”或“Assisted-By:”。

blocks.html_en: • Prior Discussion of Bulk or Automated Changes: Similarly to the mass-bug filing process (Developers Reference section 7.1.1), contributors should discuss their intention before submitting bulk or autonomously generated contributions. Any such automated process should be overseen by a human who remains accountable for its behavior and output.

sentences.en: Prior Discussion of Bulk or Automated Changes: Similarly to the mass-bug filing process (Developers Reference section 7.1.1), contributors should discuss their intention before submitting bulk or autonomously generated contributions.
sentences.zh: 批量或自动更改的事先讨论：与批量错误归档流程（开发人员参考第 7.1.1 节）类似，贡献者应在提交批量或自动生成的贡献之前讨论他们的意图。

sentences.en: Any such automated process should be overseen by a human who remains accountable for its behavior and output.
sentences.zh: 任何此类自动化流程都应由对其行为和输出负责的人员监督。

blocks.html_en: • Confidentiality and Privacy: Contributors must not use generative AI tools that transmit data to untrusted providers with non-public or sensitive project information (such as embargoed security reports or private communication), as this may lead to the unintended disclosure of confidential data.

sentences.en: Confidentiality and Privacy: Contributors must not use generative AI tools that transmit data to untrusted providers with non-public or sensitive project information (such as embargoed security reports or private communication), as this may lead to the unintended disclosure of confidential data.
sentences.zh: 保密和隐私：贡献者不得使用生成式 AI 工具将数据传输给具有非公开或敏感项目信息（例如禁运的安全报告或私人通信）的不受信任的提供商，因为这可能会导致机密数据的意外泄露。

blocks.html_en: Summary: Reject LLMs (generative "AI") as far as practical

sentences.en: Summary: Reject LLMs (generative "AI") as far as practical
sentences.zh: 摘要：尽可能拒绝法学硕士（生成式“AI”）

sentences.en: BACKGROUND
sentences.zh: 背景

blocks.html_en: LLMs have many serious problems, including: undermining the mechanisms of free software community building; environmental damage; exploitation of authors; disruption to open web hosting by aggressive scraping; generation and promulgation of bullshit; polluting the information commons; hazards to users' mental health; economic bubbles; distortion of the computer hardware market; fraud; ownership by horrible people and companies; and so on. Ethical and safe use of this technology is almost impossible.

sentences.en: LLMs have many serious problems, including: undermining the mechanisms of free software community building; environmental damage; exploitation of authors; disruption to open web hosting by aggressive scraping; generation and promulgation of bullshit; polluting the information commons; hazards to users' mental health; economic bubbles; distortion of the computer hardware market; fraud; ownership by horrible people and companies; and so on.
sentences.zh: LLM存在许多严重问题，包括：破坏自由软件社区建设机制；环境破坏；对作者的剥削；通过积极的抓取破坏开放网络托管；胡言乱语的产生和传播；污染信息共享；对用户心理健康造成危害；经济泡沫；计算机硬件市场的扭曲；欺诈罪;被可怕的人和公司所拥有；等等。

sentences.en: Ethical and safe use of this technology is almost impossible.
sentences.zh: 以道德和安全的方式使用这项技术几乎是不可能的。

blocks.html_en: Ideally, LLM output should not form any part of software that we rely on, nor should LLM output ever take the place of human-written prose.

sentences.en: Ideally, LLM output should not form any part of software that we rely on, nor should LLM output ever take the place of human-written prose.
sentences.zh: 理想情况下，LLM 输出不应构成我们所依赖的软件的任何部分，LLM 输出也不应取代人类撰写的散文。

blocks.html_en: Unfortunately some of the wider software world, including many of our upstreams, take a different view. Therefore a complete ban on LLM output as part of Debian is currently impractical.

sentences.en: Unfortunately some of the wider software world, including many of our upstreams, take a different view.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，一些更广泛的软件世界，包括我们的许多上游，持不同的观点。

sentences.en: Therefore a complete ban on LLM output as part of Debian is currently impractical.
sentences.zh: 因此，在 Debian 中完全禁止 LLM 输出目前是不切实际的。

sentences.en: REQUESTS
sentences.zh: 要求

blocks.html_en: 1. We request that all contributors to Debian avoid the use of LLMs in their Debian work.

sentences.en: We request that all contributors to Debian avoid the use of LLMs in their Debian work.
sentences.zh: 我们要求 Debian 的所有贡献者避免在他们的 Debian 工作中使用 LLM。

blocks.html_en: 2. We request that all decisionmakers within Debian discourage LLM use as much as practical. Practicality is a judgement call and we recognise that it will involve uncomfortable compromises.

sentences.en: We request that all decisionmakers within Debian discourage LLM use as much as practical.
sentences.zh: 我们要求 Debian 内部的所有决策者尽可能阻止 LLM 的使用。

sentences.en: Practicality is a judgement call and we recognise that it will involve uncomfortable compromises.
sentences.zh: 实用性是一种判断，我们认识到这将涉及令人不舒服的妥协。

blocks.html_en: 3. We request that everyone, even outside Debian, should refrain from using this technology. In particular, the Free Software and Open Source communities should reject LLMs. We recognise that not everyone will heed this call.

sentences.en: We request that everyone, even outside Debian, should refrain from using this technology.
sentences.zh: 我们要求每个人，即使是 Debian 之外的人，都不要使用这项技术。

sentences.en: In particular, the Free Software and Open Source communities should reject LLMs.
sentences.zh: 特别是，自由软件和开源社区应该拒绝法学硕士。

sentences.en: We recognise that not everyone will heed this call.
sentences.zh: 我们认识到并不是每个人都会留意这一呼吁。

sentences.en: REQUIREMENTS (SUPPLEMENT TO THE CODE OF CONDUCT)
sentences.zh: 要求（行为准则的补充）

blocks.html_en: 4. Within Debian, messages to humans (including for example bug reports, mailing list messages, discussions on Salsa, and blog posts on Planet Debian) must be drafted solely by humans without LLM assistance.

sentences.en: Within Debian, messages to humans (including for example bug reports, mailing list messages, discussions on Salsa, and blog posts on Planet Debian) must be drafted solely by humans without LLM assistance.
sentences.zh: 在 Debian 中，发送给人类的消息（包括错误报告、邮件列表消息、Salsa 讨论以及 Debian 星球上的博客文章）必须仅由人类起草，无需 LLM 协助。

blocks.html_en: 5. Any use of LLMs for Debian work must be disclosed.

sentences.en: Any use of LLMs for Debian work must be disclosed.
sentences.zh: 任何使用 LLM 进行 Debian 工作的情况都必须予以披露。

blocks.html_en: 6. Individual projects and maintainers may ban LLM contributions completely. Such bans (including by upstream projects) must be respected.

sentences.en: Individual projects and maintainers may ban LLM contributions completely.
sentences.zh: 个别项目和维护者可能会完全禁止 LLM 贡献。

sentences.en: Such bans (including by upstream projects) must be respected.
sentences.zh: 必须遵守此类禁令（包括上游项目的禁令）。

blocks.html_en: 7. Violations of these requirements should be treated as violations of the Code of Conduct and should result in swift but proportionate disciplinary action.

sentences.en: Violations of these requirements should be treated as violations of the Code of Conduct and should result in swift but proportionate disciplinary action.
sentences.zh: 违反这些要求应被视为违反行为准则，并应导致迅速但相称的纪律处分。

blocks.html_en: 8. Any contributor who feels they cannot write in English without assistance, may write in their native language, and expect readers to use translation tools of their choice. In that case a human-written English summary would be very welcome but is not required. In any case we promise not to shame anyone for any linguistic mistakes.

sentences.en: Any contributor who feels they cannot write in English without assistance, may write in their native language, and expect readers to use translation tools of their choice.
sentences.zh: 任何认为自己无法在没有帮助的情况下用英语写作的贡献者都可以用自己的母语写作，并期望读者使用他们选择的翻译工具。

sentences.en: In that case a human-written English summary would be very welcome but is not required.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，人工编写的英文摘要将非常受欢迎，但不是必需的。

sentences.en: In any case we promise not to shame anyone for any linguistic mistakes.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，我们保证不会因为任何语言错误而羞辱任何人。

sentences.en: Debian as a project does not endorse or recommend the use of generative AI assistants for software development, as it raises multiple concerns about ethics, legality, copyright, etc.

blocks.html_en: Nevertheless, Debian acknowledges that these practices are already in use and here to stay. Rather than banning their use, which seems counter-productive and unenforceable, the project chooses to place responsibility on contributors and therefore defines the following guidelines.

sentences.en: Nevertheless, Debian acknowledges that these practices are already in use and here to stay.

blocks.html_en: These apply exclusively to code and work done specifically for the Debian project (Debian websites, applications, resources, packages, etc.). They do not apply to any upstream work. In what follows, "work" refers to the contributions done specifically for the Debian project.

sentences.en: These apply exclusively to code and work done specifically for the Debian project (Debian websites, applications, resources, packages, etc.).

提案A

选择1

前言

该提案旨在明确禁止任何使用或协助大型语言模型 (LLM) 或其他生成式 AI 工具编写的对 Debian 的贡献。

本全球报告的范围是（非详尽）：

  • Debian 源码包
  • 官方Debian项目软件，如lintian
  • Debian 网络资源
  • 由 Debian 贡献者添加的文档和翻译
  • 来自 Debian 的官方通讯

它不包括：

  • 使用法学硕士进行开发的上游项目
  • AI相关软件
  • 上游补丁/安全修复等。

基本原理

Debian 因其稳定性而享有盛誉。 这种稳定性对于 Debian 在自由软件生态系统中的地位至关重要。 我们相信，LLM 的广泛使用来自于“快速行动，打破常规”的态度，这种态度虽然在该行业的许多部分很常见，但与 Debian 的本质背道而驰，并且对于 Debian 贡献者来说是不合适的。

实际上，LLM 的使用引起了以下问题：

1. 版权

LLM输出的法律地位非常不明确：可能根据其本身的优点获得版权，也可能不获得版权；它可能会受到训练数据中所有许可和版权的影响，也可能不会。 Debian 政策和 DFSG 要求许可和版权绝对清晰[1][2]。 Debian 不允许由版权或许可状态不明确的人以传统方式编写的软件和其他贡献； LLM 输出不应对此有特殊例外。

2. 质量

LLM输出存在许多众所周知的准确性问题。[3][4][5]法学硕士永远无法“知道”其输出是否正确，因为它仅产生语法上可能的训练数据组合。 在某些环境中这已经足够好了。 在 Debian 中，情况并非如此。 例如，在打包方面，每个 Debian 源码包都是独一无二的。 由于打包语法和最佳实践随着时间的推移而发生变化，LLM 生成的包将包含跨越存档时代的内容的混合体，其中包含不起作用的监视文件、断章取义的覆盖、虚构的版权，并且通常不适合上传。 具有打包专业知识的经验丰富的 Debian 贡献者可能会发现这里的一些有限的用处，但新的贡献者不能，也不知道如何修复它。 这些相同的质量和准确性问题显然适用于上述提案范围中列出的所有领域。 如果 Debian 是一个封闭的组织，仅由永不离开的领域专家组成，那么这可能不是问题；然而，

3. 社区

Debian 是一个不仅仅是代码的项目：它是一个建立在对自由软件和解决技术问题的共同兴趣之上的社区。 Debian 有意识地通过多种方式发展这个社区，并且总是鼓励新的贡献者加入。 允许法学硕士捐款打破了这一点。 新的贡献者提交法学硕士输出以供审阅会给审阅者带来不必要的压力，这可能会导致倦怠。 此外，依赖 LLM 的新贡献者实际上并没有学习和理解 Debian 打包或流程的细节，因此他们无法取代以前精疲力尽的 DD。

4. 伦理

LLM 公司通过抓取整个网络来获取训练数据，直接损害了整个自由软件社区，而不考虑许可证、版权，甚至没有考虑到 robots.txt 等既定惯例。[6]这对 Debian 的公共网络资源产生了重大负面影响，对许多用户依赖的网站造成了大规模且永久的拒绝服务攻击。 因此，我们的基础设施的某些部分根本无法访问，并且必须启用基于 JS 的检查。 许多其他项目也受到类似影响。 此外，LLM培训消耗的资源数量惊人[7]，而我们为了保护而被迫实施的用户验证系统也浪费了资源。 这是对互联网作为公共资源的公然漠视，浪费了系统管理员的时间，虽然个别LLM课程不直接使用大量资源或DoS公共网络，但它们完全可以使用的事实是LLM公司这些不道德行为的直接结果。

Debian 有社会契约。 [8] 我们的首要任务是我们的用户和自由软件。 Debian 很稳定。 [9] 用户和组织选择 Debian 是因为它可靠且安全。

Debian 并不是为了生成尽可能多的代码（需要由数量不断减少的人类志愿者进行手动审查），或者打包每个软件，或者急于推出新功能，但这正是 LLM 的用途。

总之，允许LLM贡献有悖于社会契约，也违背了创建注重质量和稳定性的自由操作系统的共同事业。

提议

为了不损害 Debian 的声誉或进一步损害社区，应禁止 LLM 协助的贡献包含在 Debian 中。

尽管我们的立场是 LLM 贡献与 Debian 已批准的文件相矛盾，但为了消除所有疑虑，我们建议对社会契约添加以下内容：

6. Works Created through the use of Large Language Models (LLMs)

We will not
allow direct contributions to Debian written with the use or assistance of large
language models (LLMs) or other generative AI tools. Direct contributions are
defined as packaging, native Debian software like lintian, documentation and
translations written by Debian contributors, and official Debian web resources,
etc. Other categories such as upstream projects written with LLM assistance may
be included at a later date. This ensures that Debian remains a stable, trusted,
and reliable operating system, and protects the interests of the Debian
volunteers who make it possible.

可能的问题

其他探索类似决定的项目也得到了一个共同的答复：“你们将如何执行对法学硕士捐款的禁令？” 虽然执行可能是一个挑战，但这是 Debian 社区的意向声明，我们相信该社区会真诚地遵守它。

允许人工智能辅助贡献

该项目利用宪法第 4.1 (5) 条赋予的权力，发布以下声明，描述其当前对人工智能辅助贡献的立场。 本声明描述了该项目在通过时的立场。 这一立场可能会随着时间的推移而演变，而无需诉诸未来的一般性决议。 如果项目需要做出决定但无法达成共识，GR 流程仍然可用。

Debian 项目认识到人工智能辅助的贡献引起了许多担忧，例如关于此类贡献的技术质量和可维护性及其法律地位。 人工智能本身也引发了额外的担忧，即它对整个社会、IT 行业和自由软件的影响；关于其对环境的影响；以及人工智能抓取工具的攻击性或不合规做法。

尽管如此，许多 Debian 贡献者发现人工智能工具在为 Debian 做出贡献并最终改进 Debian 时很有帮助。

考虑到人工智能辅助的好处和风险，以及社区内有争议的讨论，Debian 项目认为有必要澄清其对人工智能辅助贡献的立场并建立明确的指导方针。

Debian 项目允许人工智能辅助贡献（部分或全部由法学硕士生成），前提是满足以下条件：

  1. 工具法律兼容性：贡献者应确保生成式 AI 工具的条款和条件不会施加与 Debian 环境中输出的分发、修改或使用相冲突的合同限制。
  2. 许可和归属：如果人工智能工具的输出中包含由第三方创作或拥有的任何预先存在的受版权保护的材料（包括作为免费软件许可的预先存在的代码），则在将此类输出贡献给项目之前，贡献者应验证他们有权根据相关开源许可提交该输出。
  3. 责任：贡献者对其贡献承担全部责任，包括保证其提交内容的技术优点、安全性、许可证合规性和实用性。 贡献者仍然对全部这些贡献承担全部责任。 贡献者应充分理解提议的更改并准备好证明其合理性。
  4. 披露：当贡献的很大一部分是由工具生成或实质协助时，贡献者应披露该工具的使用情况，使其对目标受众清晰可见。 这涵盖了所有形式的贡献，包括代码、邮件列表帖子和错误讨论。 披露的形式由贡献者决定；一种方便的提交选项是 Git 预告片，例如“Generate-By:”或“Assisted-By:”。
  5. 批量或自动更改的事先讨论：与批量错误归档流程（开发人员参考第 7.1.1 节）类似，贡献者应在提交批量或自动生成的贡献之前讨论他们的意图。 任何此类自动化流程都应由对其行为和输出负责的人员监督。
  6. 保密和隐私：贡献者不得使用生成式 AI 工具将数据传输给具有非公开或敏感项目信息（例如禁运的安全报告或私人通信）的不受信任的提供商，因为这可能会导致机密数据的意外泄露。

摘要：尽可能拒绝法学硕士（生成式“AI”）

背景

LLM存在许多严重问题，包括：破坏自由软件社区建设机制；环境破坏；对作者的剥削；通过积极的抓取破坏开放网络托管；胡言乱语的产生和传播；污染信息共享；对用户心理健康造成危害；经济泡沫；计算机硬件市场的扭曲；欺诈罪;被可怕的人和公司所拥有；等等。 以道德和安全的方式使用这项技术几乎是不可能的。

理想情况下，LLM 输出不应构成我们所依赖的软件的任何部分，LLM 输出也不应取代人类撰写的散文。

不幸的是，一些更广泛的软件世界，包括我们的许多上游，持不同的观点。 因此，在 Debian 中完全禁止 LLM 输出目前是不切实际的。

要求

1. 我们要求 Debian 的所有贡献者避免在他们的 Debian 工作中使用 LLM。

2. 我们要求 Debian 内部的所有决策者尽可能阻止 LLM 的使用。 实用性是一种判断，我们认识到这将涉及令人不舒服的妥协。

3. 我们要求每个人，即使是 Debian 之外的人，都不要使用这项技术。 特别是，自由软件和开源社区应该拒绝法学硕士。 我们认识到并不是每个人都会留意这一呼吁。

要求（行为准则的补充）

4. 在 Debian 中，发送给人类的消息（包括错误报告、邮件列表消息、Salsa 讨论以及 Debian 星球上的博客文章）必须仅由人类起草，无需 LLM 协助。

5. 任何使用 LLM 进行 Debian 工作的情况都必须予以披露。

6. 个别项目和维护者可能会完全禁止 LLM 贡献。 必须遵守此类禁令（包括上游项目的禁令）。

7. 违反这些要求应被视为违反行为准则，并应导致迅速但相称的纪律处分。

8. 任何认为自己无法在没有帮助的情况下用英语写作的贡献者都可以用自己的母语写作，并期望读者使用他们选择的翻译工具。 在这种情况下，人工编写的英文摘要将非常受欢迎，但不是必需的。 无论如何，我们保证不会因为任何语言错误而羞辱任何人。

提案D

选择4

接受 AI 对 Debian 特定工作的贡献

Debian 作为一个项目并不认可或推荐使用生成式 AI 助手进行软件开发，因为它引发了对道德、合法性、版权等方面的多重担忧。

尽管如此，Debian 承认这些做法已经在使用并且将继续存在。 该项目并没有禁止它们的使用，这似乎会适得其反且无法执行，而是选择将责任归咎于贡献者，因此定义了以下准则。

这些仅适用于专门为 Debian 项目（Debian 网站、应用程序、资源、软件包等）完成的代码和工作。 它们不适用于任何上游工作。 在下文中，“工作”指的是专门为 Debian 项目所做的贡献。

  • 由生成式 AI 代理或工具辅助的所有代码和工作都必须符合 DFSG。
  • 提交者对所提交的作品承担全部责任，并且：对拟提交的作品进行了充分的评估和正确的理解，并能够对其进行解释和辩护；他们将任何潜在的 Signed-off-by 标签和 GPG 签名放在发送给 Debian 基础设施的贡献上（包、提交、邮件……） 他们自己；任何最终将在 Debian 基础设施（主 git 分支、包上传）上生产的上传内容均已由他们明确提交。
  • 由生成式人工智能代理或工具辅助的工作应在适当的位置进行标记（提交消息、变更日志等）。 一些轻量级的生成工具，例如 Copilot 中的制表符补全，可能会在贡献者没有意识到他们依赖生成式 AI 模型的情况下使用；因此，我们相信提交者能够评估该规则何时适用。 如有疑问，请添加此类标记；
  • 当传输的数据可能对项目敏感时（个人数据、禁运信息……），不得使用基于云的人工智能 或不公开（debian 私人讨论，...）。
